title: Control cardinality + query latency for unit economics drilldowns (pre-aggregations, caching, query guardrails)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Background / why this exists
- The unit economics dashboard is intended to be the source of truth for blended cost ($/1M output tokens) and needs interactive drilldowns by model, region, and tier.
- Early spike tests showed query latency and cost ballooning when users combined multiple high-cardinality dimensions (model_variant + region + customer_tier + quantization_profile + runtime_config + route_id), especially on 90-day ranges.
- We need guardrails + the right pre-aggregations so Console stays fast and we don’t DDOS the warehouse.

Goals
- Keep interactive drilldowns fast enough for weekly review workflows (Finance/Product) and ad-hoc Eng investigations.
- Prevent unbounded cardinality combinations and “accidental full scans”.
- Make performance behavior predictable and documented (what’s supported, what gets auto-rolled-up).

Non-goals
- Building a general-purpose OLAP cube for arbitrary dimensions.
- Supporting per-customer/account drilldowns in the MVP dashboard.

Current behavior (as of 2025-02-10)
- Backend endpoints in ENG-2915 query the semantic layer view (see PR-11857) and apply filters as requested.
- No strong query guardrails beyond basic date range constraints.
- No server-side result caching; repeated loads of the same slice re-run the same query.

Proposed approach
1) Pre-aggregations / rollups (warehouse-side)
- Add curated rollup tables (or materialized views) at daily grain aligned to the supported dashboard drilldowns.
- Recommended rollups (names illustrative; align to existing unit_econ schema from ENG-2910):
  a) unit_econ_daily_by_model_region_tier
     - keys: day, model_family, model_variant, region, customer_tier
     - measures: blended_cost_usd, output_tokens, blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens, cache_hit_rate, estimated_cache_savings_usd, overhead_alloc_usd
  b) unit_econ_daily_by_model_region (tier rolled up)
  c) unit_econ_daily_by_region_tier (model rolled up)
  d) unit_econ_daily_overall (model + region + tier rolled up)
- For “optional” dimensions (quantization_profile, runtime_config):
  - Do not pre-aggregate across all values initially.
  - Support slicing by these dimensions only when constrained to (a) a single model_variant and (b) a short date range (default <= 14 days), OR via a Top-N endpoint (see guardrails).

2) Query guardrails (backend API)
- Hard limits (return 400 with actionable error copy):
  - Max date range for high-cardinality queries: 31 days when grouping by quantization_profile OR runtime_config OR route_id.
  - Disallow grouping by both quantization_profile AND runtime_config in the same request (too many combinations; forces a cross-product and yields low-actionability charts).
  - Max group-by cardinality: 200 groups returned (server enforces ORDER BY output_tokens DESC, then truncates to top 200 + “Other”).
  - Max rows returned for table export endpoints: 5,000 (require tighter filters for more).
- Soft limits (auto-behavior):
  - If user selects “All models” and “All tiers”, backend auto-routes to unit_econ_daily_by_region_tier or unit_econ_daily_overall depending on selected breakdown.
  - For 90-day view, default chart uses weekly bucketing (server-side) unless user is in a tightly-filtered slice.

3) Server-side caching (query results)
- Implement result cache in the dashboard backend:
  - Cache key = normalized query JSON (filters + grain + breakdown + requested measures) + semantic layer version.
  - TTL: 60s for interactive chart queries; 10m for “weekly review” stable views; 0 for export/download endpoints (to avoid confusion on stale exports).
  - Cache store: Redis (shared), with size-based eviction.
- Add instrumentation:
  - cache_hit, cache_miss, cache_stale_refresh counts
  - query_runtime_ms, bytes_scanned (if available), rows_returned

4) Performance test plan
- Define a small suite of representative queries (run in CI or nightly):
  - Overall blended cost, 90d, weekly buckets
  - By model_variant + region + tier, 30d
  - By region + tier, 90d
  - Constrained quantization_profile slice, single model_variant, 14d
- Track p50/p95 query latency and warehouse cost (if available) and alert on regressions.

Acceptance criteria
- API performance (measured on staging with prod-like partitions; documented dataset sizes):
  - p95 < 1.5s for default dashboard load (overall + top model table, last 30d)
  - p95 < 3.0s for common drilldown (model_variant + region + tier, last 30d)
  - p95 < 5.0s for 90d views that use weekly bucketing
- Guardrails:
  - Requests exceeding defined limits fail fast with clear UI copy (Design ticket DES-211 covers error states; coordinate exact messaging).
  - No endpoint allows grouping that can produce >200 groups without truncation and “Other”.
- Caching:
  - Achieve >40% cache hit rate on repeated navigation within a 10-minute window during internal dogfooding.
- Documentation:
  - Add a short “Supported drilldowns + limits” section to the dashboard internal docs and link from the Console page.

Implementation notes / open questions
- Warehouse choice for rollups: implement in the same place as the semantic layer (PR-11857). Prefer incremental daily partitions to avoid full rebuilds.
- “Other” bucket definition: must be consistent across charts/tables (same sorting metric: output_tokens DESC). Ensure totals reconcile (sum(groups)+Other = total).
- Late arriving data: rollups need to support backfill/recompute of the last N days (recommend N=3) without breaking caches (cache key should include a semantic layer version + effective data watermark).
- Export behavior: exports should include the truncated vs full note (we should probably block exports when truncation occurs unless user applies tighter filters).

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/internal-unit-economics-dashboard-prd.json
- Data contracts: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/unit-economics-dashboard-data-contracts.json
- Canonical metric ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0142-blended-cost-per-1m-output-tokens-definition.json
- Backend endpoints: ENG-2915

Risks
- Over-constraining drilldowns reduces usefulness for Eng investigations; mitigate by providing a Top-N “advanced” path and a documented process for one-off deep dives.
- Pre-aggregations may drift from base tables if late data/backfills aren’t handled consistently; must align with ENG-2914 reconciliation and the backfill runbook.

Definition of done
- Rollup tables/views exist, are used by backend for the main dashboard paths, and are included in the semantic layer docs.
- Guardrails implemented and covered by unit tests (request normalization + limit enforcement).
- Caching shipped behind the internal feature flag and metrics confirm expected hit rate.
- Load test suite is in place and has baseline numbers recorded.
comments: 2025-02-11 (Thomas Baird): I pulled query logs from staging. The worst offenders are “group by quantization_profile” across 90d plus model_variant (thousands of groups). +1 on hard-disallowing quant_profile + runtime_config together; we should also clamp quant_profile views to a single model_variant and <=14d.

2025-02-12 (Chloe Martin): Backend already normalizes filters; adding a query hash for Redis is straightforward. One concern: need to include semantic layer version / watermark in the cache key to avoid serving stale results after backfills.

2025-02-14 (Caleb Johnson): For truncation/Other bucket, please make sure totals reconcile and the UI indicates that it’s truncated. We’ve had confusion on other dashboards where people export the truncated table and assume it’s complete.

2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Aligning on supported rollups: overall, by model+region+tier, and by region+tier are must-have. Quant/runtime_config slices can be “advanced” and limited. Finance review is mostly using overall + model mix + region mix.

2025-02-21 (Thomas Baird): Implemented draft guardrails locally (max 31d for quant/runtime breakdown; top-200 groups). Next step is wiring rollup selection logic so we don’t hit the base view for the default path. Will post benchmark numbers once rollups land.
